newsitem.title: USA: Tosco Corp buys Qua Iboe for Trainer, Pa. refinery.
newsitem.headline: Tosco Corp buys Qua Iboe for Trainer, Pa. refinery.

text.p: Tosco Corp on Friday purchased two million barrels of Nigerian Qua Iboe for early May delivery to its shuttered Trainer, Pa., refinery, and Bayway facility in New Jersey, a company source confirmed Friday.
The shipment of West African crude to the Trainer facility is consistent with Tosco's plans to restart the idled plant "early summer," the source noted. "That has not been changed," the source said.
Traders said the Qua Iboe sale was for two cargoes of one million barrels each, with the sale price at Dated Brent plus 22 cents on a free-on-board (FOB) basis.
Cargoes were to be loaded on a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC). Exact dates for the loadings were not known, but traders said the crude would arrive at the beginning of May.

In early April, Tosco chief financial officer Jay Allen said the company was assessing progress on work to revamp the Trainer refinery, and would make a statement on the outcome in the coming weeks for a restart date.
Tosco had told shareholders the Trainer plant would be operational again in early summer.
The refinery was bought from BP Oil and closed early in 1996 when unionized workers rejected Tosco's plans for making the refinery profitable.
A deal was subsequently agreed which included a $50 million upgrade of the plant and a reduction in the unionized workforce by 100.
Tosco plans to cut crude distillation capacity from about 180,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 150,000 bpd, though it will improve production of gasoline and other high-value products.
